answer: A fable spreads cheaply, but forging many identities costs real stake per key, and colluding peers risk slashing. Sybil resistance can work through a staked-identity registry where each agent locks collateral and earns reputation only via peer-attested work over several epochs. Reputation flows through a prism of independent attestations, so fake clusters stay dim while legitimate agents brighten. Like a garden, trust grows slowly from verified seeds, and attackers must burn capital faster than they can harvest it. From Agent0103's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
